words.enDefinition: The full group that a statistical study aims to describe or draw conclusions about.

examples.en: The target population includes every student enrolled in the fictional university during the autumn term.
examples.zh: 「目标总体」包括这所虚构大学秋季学期注册的所有学生。

examples.en: We defined the target population before choosing the records available for the classroom survey.
examples.zh: 我们先界定「目标总体」，再挑选课堂调查能使用的记录。

words.enDefinition: The list or other representation used to identify units available for selection into a sample.

examples.en: The sampling frame lists the households eligible for selection in our fictional district survey.
examples.zh: 「抽样框」列出虚构地区调查中可被抽中的各户家庭。

examples.en: We checked whether the sampling frame omitted households in the newly built part of town.
examples.zh: 我们检查「抽样框」是否漏掉了镇上新建区域的住户。

words.enDefinition: An individual element or group selected at a stage of a sampling design.

examples.en: The sampling unit is a classroom when the first draw selects entire classes in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习第一轮抽取整个班级时，「抽样单位」就是班级。

examples.en: We identified the sampling unit before counting how many selections were made at each stage.
examples.zh: 我们先确定「抽样单位」，再统计各阶段的抽取次数。

words.enDefinition: For a fixed-size sample, the number selected divided by the number of units in the population or stratum.

examples.en: The sampling fraction is one fifth because the exercise selects twenty of the hundred records.
examples.zh: 练习从一百条记录中抽取二十条，因此「抽样比」为五分之一。

examples.en: We compared the sampling fraction used for the two groups in the fictional school survey.
examples.zh: 我们比较了虚构学校调查中两组所用的「抽样比」。

words.enDefinition: A sample selected by a design in which every population unit has a known or calculable positive probability of selection.

examples.en: The exercise uses a probability sample so each household has a known chance of selection.
examples.zh: 练习使用「概率样本」，使每户家庭被抽中的概率已知。

examples.en: We discussed why a probability sample helps the analyst account for the design when estimating uncertainty.
examples.zh: 我们讨论为什么「概率样本」有助于分析者在估计不确定性时考虑抽样设计。

words.enDefinition: A fixed-size sample for which all possible subsets of that size are equally likely under sampling without replacement.

examples.en: The simple random sample contains four records drawn from the same complete list in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中的「简单随机样本」包含从同一份完整名单抽出的四条记录。

examples.en: We used a simple random sample to illustrate why different draws can give different means.
examples.zh: 我们用「简单随机样本」说明不同的抽取结果为何可能产生不同均值。

words.enDefinition: A design that divides the population into disjoint groups and selects a random sample within each group.

examples.en: The class used stratified random sampling to include observations from each grade in the fictional school.
examples.zh: 全班用「分层随机抽样」纳入虚构学校各年级的观测。

examples.en: We compared stratified random sampling with drawing one sample from the entire list at once.
examples.zh: 我们将「分层随机抽样」与一次性从完整名单抽样作了比较。

collocations: design a stratified random sampling scheme

words.enDefinition: A design that randomly selects groups of units and then observes units in the selected groups.

examples.en: The exercise uses cluster sampling by drawing schools first and surveying classes in the selected schools.
examples.zh: 练习采用「整群抽样」，先抽取学校，再对抽中学校的班级进行调查。

examples.en: We discussed why students from one school can resemble one another more under cluster sampling.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么「整群抽样」中同校学生彼此可能更相似。

words.enDefinition: A design that takes every specified number of units from an ordered list after a random start.

examples.en: Systematic sampling chooses every tenth record after a random starting point in our classroom example.
examples.zh: 在课堂示例中，「系统抽样」从随机起点开始，每十条抽取一条记录。

examples.en: We checked the ordering of the list before applying systematic sampling to the fictional records.
examples.zh: 我们先核对名单的排列顺序，再对虚构记录做「系统抽样」。

words.enDefinition: A sample selected from units that are easy to reach or willing to participate without a probability design.

examples.en: The convenience sample contains only visitors who happened to enter the library during the lunch hour.
examples.zh: 「便利样本」只包含碰巧在午餐时段进图书馆的访客。

examples.en: We discussed what a convenience sample could miss in the classroom exercise on student travel.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了学生出行课堂练习中的「便利样本」可能会漏掉哪些人。

words.enDefinition: A sampling problem in which part of the target population is missing or inadequately represented in the frame.

examples.en: The exercise illustrates undercoverage because the list excludes students living outside the university residences.
examples.zh: 练习的名单排除了不住校的学生，因此出现「覆盖不足」。

examples.en: We drew a diagram showing which households are affected by undercoverage in the sample frame.
examples.zh: 我们画示意图，标出哪些家庭受到抽样框「覆盖不足」的影响。

words.enDefinition: A systematic error that can arise when respondents differ from nonrespondents on the characteristic being estimated.

examples.en: Nonresponse bias could arise if the students with the longest commutes seldom answer the survey.
examples.zh: 如果通勤时间最长的学生很少回答问卷，就可能出现「无应答偏差」。

examples.en: We considered nonresponse bias before interpreting the average travel time in the classroom survey.
examples.zh: 我们先考虑「无应答偏差」，再解释课堂调查得到的平均出行时间。

words.enDefinition: A systematic error caused by people choosing to respond in ways related to the topic or outcome.

examples.en: The class discussed voluntary response bias because students with strong opinions were more likely to participate.
examples.zh: 全班讨论了「自愿应答偏差」，因为意见强烈的学生更可能参与。

examples.en: We examined whether voluntary response bias could distort satisfaction results from the open online survey.
examples.zh: 我们考察「自愿应答偏差」会不会让开放式网络调查的满意度结果失真。

words.enDefinition: The deviation of a sample estimate from its population value arising because only a sample was observed.

examples.en: The sampling error changes across repeated draws even when the population mean stays fixed.
examples.zh: 即使总体均值保持不变，各次抽取的「抽样误差」也会变化。

examples.en: We illustrated sampling error by comparing each simulated survey estimate with the known population value.
examples.zh: 我们把各次模拟调查的估计值与已知总体值比较，以说明「抽样误差」。

words.enDefinition: The distribution of a statistic across all samples that could be drawn using the same design.

examples.en: The sampling distribution shows how the sample mean varies across repeated draws of the same size.
examples.zh: 「抽样分布」显示样本均值如何随同一样本量的反复抽取而变化。

examples.en: We approximated the sampling distribution by repeating the classroom sampling exercise many times on simulated data.
examples.zh: 我们在模拟数据上反复进行课堂抽样练习，以近似得到「抽样分布」。

words.enDefinition: The sum of the observed numerical values divided by the number of values in the sample.

examples.en: The sample mean changes when the class draws a different set of observations from the same list.
examples.zh: 全班从同一名单抽出另一组观测时，「样本均值」发生变化。

examples.en: We used the sample mean as one estimate of the centre of the fictional population.
examples.zh: 我们用「样本均值」来估计虚构总体的中心位置。

collocations: sampling distribution of the sample mean

words.enDefinition: The fraction of sampled observations with the characteristic of interest.

examples.en: The sample proportion is the number of students who cycle divided by the total number surveyed.
examples.zh: 「样本比例」用骑自行车的学生人数除以受访学生总数得到。

examples.en: We recorded the sample proportion from each simulated draw before examining how much it varied.
examples.zh: 我们记下各次模拟抽取的「样本比例」，再检查它的变动幅度。

collocations: sampling distribution of a sample proportion

words.enDefinition: A measure of squared spread around the sample mean, commonly using the sample size minus one as divisor.

examples.en: The sample variance is larger for the group whose scores are more spread out in our example.
examples.zh: 示例中，成绩分布更分散的组，其「样本方差」更大。

examples.en: We calculated the sample variance by dividing the squared deviation sum by the sample size minus one.
examples.zh: 我们把离均差平方和除以样本量减一，得到「样本方差」。

words.enDefinition: A numerical characteristic of a population that a statistical analysis seeks to describe or estimate.

examples.en: The population parameter in our example is the true average travel time for all students.
examples.zh: 示例中的「总体参数」是全体学生真实的平均出行时间。

examples.en: We treated the population parameter as fixed while repeating the simulated sampling exercise in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上反复进行模拟抽样时，我们把「总体参数」视为固定值。

words.enDefinition: A number calculated from sample observations alone.

examples.en: The sample statistic is calculated from the responses of the students actually drawn for the survey.
examples.zh: 「样本统计量」用实际抽中学生的回答计算得出。

examples.en: We used the median as a sample statistic to describe the survey responses in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们用中位数作为「样本统计量」来描述调查回答。

collocations: observed value of a sample statistic

words.enDefinition: A rule that uses sample data to produce one numerical estimate of a parameter.

examples.en: The point estimator takes each classroom sample and returns a single value for the population mean.
examples.zh: 「点估计量」对每个课堂样本都给出一个总体均值的数值估计。

examples.en: We compared two formulas to decide which point estimator varied less across the repeated samples.
examples.zh: 我们比较两种公式，确定哪一个「点估计量」在重复抽样中的波动较小。

words.enDefinition: The particular numerical estimate obtained by applying a point estimator to observed data.

examples.en: The point estimate changes when we draw a new sample from the same fictional population.
examples.zh: 从同一虚构总体重新抽样时，「点估计值」会变化。

examples.en: We reported the point estimate beside the interval to distinguish the single value from the range.
examples.zh: 我们将「点估计值」与区间并列报告，区分单个数值和数值范围。

words.enDefinition: The expected value of an estimator minus the parameter it is intended to estimate.

examples.en: Estimator bias is positive when the estimates average above the true value in our simulation.
examples.zh: 模拟中，当各次估计的平均值高于真值时，「估计量偏差」为正。

examples.en: We compared estimator bias across two formulas using many repeated samples of the same size.
examples.zh: 我们用许多同样大小的重复样本比较两种公式的「估计量偏差」。

words.enDefinition: An estimator whose expected value equals the parameter for the sampling process under consideration.

examples.en: The unbiased estimator gives the correct value on average across repeated samples in the classroom illustration.
examples.zh: 在课堂示例的反复抽样中，「无偏估计量」给出平均意义下的正确值。

examples.en: We showed that an unbiased estimator may still give a poor result in one particular sample.
examples.zh: 我们说明，即使是「无偏估计量」，在某个特定样本里也可能给出较差的结果。

words.enDefinition: An estimator that converges in probability to the target as sample size grows under stated conditions.

examples.en: A consistent estimator gives values increasingly concentrated near the target in the classroom simulation.
examples.zh: 课堂模拟中，样本量越大，「一致估计量」给出的值越集中在目标值附近。

examples.en: We discussed why a consistent estimator may still be biased for a small sample.
examples.zh: 我们讨论为什么「一致估计量」在小样本下仍可能有偏。

words.enDefinition: A measure of precision comparing variances of estimators for the same target under specified conditions.

examples.en: The lesson on estimator efficiency compares how much two unbiased rules vary across repeated samples.
examples.zh: 「估计量效率」这一课比较两个无偏估计规则在反复抽样中波动有多大。

examples.en: We discussed estimator efficiency only after confirming that both formulas estimate the same population quantity.
examples.zh: 我们先确认两种公式估计的是同一个总体数值，再讨论「估计量效率」。

words.enDefinition: The standard deviation of an estimator's sampling distribution.

examples.en: The standard error of an estimator describes how much its values vary from sample to sample.
examples.zh: 「估计量的标准误」描述该估计量在不同样本之间的波动程度。

examples.en: We compared the standard error of an estimator with the spread of individual observations in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，我们比较了「估计量的标准误」和个体观测值的离散程度。

collocations: derive the standard error of an estimator
estimate the standard error of an estimator
compare the standard error of an estimator

words.enDefinition: The standard deviation of the sampling distribution of a sample mean.
acceptedEnVariants: standard error of the sample mean

examples.en: The standard error of the mean decreases when we average more independent readings in the simulation.
examples.zh: 模拟中，纳入平均计算的独立读数越多，「均值的标准误」越小。

examples.en: We estimated the standard error of the mean using the sample spread and the sample size.
examples.zh: 我们根据样本的离散程度和样本量估计「均值的标准误」。

collocations: compute the standard error of the mean
report the standard error of the mean
estimated standard error of the mean

words.enDefinition: An adjustment that reduces estimated sampling variability for draws without replacement from a finite population.

examples.en: The finite population correction matters here because the exercise samples nearly half of the available records.
examples.zh: 练习抽取了近一半可用记录，因此这里的「有限总体修正」很重要。

examples.en: We compared the estimated standard errors with and without the finite population correction in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们比较使用和未使用「有限总体修正」算出的标准误。

words.enDefinition: A number reflecting the independent information remaining after constraints, often used to specify a reference distribution.

examples.en: The degrees of freedom for this sample variance equal the sample size minus one.
examples.zh: 这个样本方差的「自由度」等于样本量减一。

examples.en: We checked the degrees of freedom before selecting a critical value from the reference table.
examples.zh: 我们先核对「自由度」，再从参考表选取临界值。

collocations: degrees of freedom for a test

words.enDefinition: A method that estimates parameters by matching sample moments to the corresponding model moments.

examples.en: The method of moments equates the sample mean to its model expectation in this example.
examples.zh: 示例里的「矩估计法」令样本均值等于对应的模型期望。

examples.en: We used the method of moments to estimate two parameters from two sample quantities.
examples.zh: 我们用「矩估计法」，根据两个样本统计量估计两个参数。

collocations: estimate by the method of moments

words.enDefinition: The joint density or mass of the observed data treated as a function of the model parameters.

examples.en: The likelihood function compares different parameter values with the observed sample held fixed in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，「似然函数」在保持观测样本不变的情况下比较不同参数值。

examples.en: We plotted the likelihood function to see which parameter values make the recorded data more plausible.
examples.zh: 我们画出「似然函数」，查看哪些参数值更能解释记录的数据。

words.enDefinition: The natural logarithm of the likelihood, with the same maximizers where the likelihood is positive.

examples.en: The log-likelihood turns the product of positive contributions into a sum in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 课堂示例中的「对数似然」将各正贡献项的乘积化成和。

examples.en: We calculated the log-likelihood for several candidate values before finding its maximum on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们先算出几个候选值对应的「对数似然」，再在练习上找它的最大值。

words.enDefinition: An estimator obtained by selecting parameter values that maximize the likelihood of the observed data.

examples.en: The maximum likelihood estimator selects the proportion that gives the largest likelihood for the observed outcomes.
examples.zh: 「最大似然估计量」选出使观测结果似然最大的比例。

examples.en: We derived a maximum likelihood estimator for the unknown success probability in our classroom model.
examples.zh: 我们推导出一个「最大似然估计量」，用来估计课堂模型中的未知成功概率。

collocations: consistency of a maximum likelihood estimator

words.enDefinition: An estimator that replaces unknown quantities in a parameter formula with estimates or sample analogues.

examples.en: The plug-in estimator substitutes the sample proportions into the formula for the target quantity in our exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中的「代入估计量」把样本比例代入目标量的公式。

examples.en: We formed a plug-in estimator after finding a suitable estimate for each unknown input.
examples.zh: 我们为各个未知输入找到合适的估计后，构造了一个「代入估计量」。

collocations: plug-in estimator for a function of parameters

words.enDefinition: Using sample information to give a range that expresses uncertainty about a population parameter.

examples.en: The interval estimation exercise gives a range for the unknown average instead of a single value.
examples.zh: 「区间估计」练习为未知平均值给出一个范围。

examples.en: We used interval estimation to show how uncertainty changes between the two classroom sample sizes.
examples.zh: 我们用「区间估计」展示两种课堂样本量下的不确定性变化。

words.enDefinition: An interval calculated by a method designed to cover a fixed population parameter at a specified long-run rate.

examples.en: The confidence interval for the mean is narrower when the class uses a larger sample.
examples.zh: 全班使用更大样本时，均值的「置信区间」更窄。

examples.en: We drew a confidence interval around each estimate to compare their precision in the simulation.
examples.zh: 我们为每个估计值画出「置信区间」，比较它们在模拟中的精确度。

words.enDefinition: The stated long-run target rate at which a confidence interval procedure captures the true parameter.

examples.en: The confidence level is ninety-five percent in the classroom exercise with repeated sampling.
examples.zh: 课堂重复抽样练习的「置信水平」为百分之九十五。

examples.en: We increased the confidence level and examined how the interval width changed on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们提高「置信水平」，观察练习纸上的区间宽度如何变化。

words.enDefinition: The actual probability under repeated sampling that an interval procedure contains the true parameter.

examples.en: The coverage probability in the simulation is estimated by counting intervals that contain the known mean.
examples.zh: 模拟里，统计包含已知均值的区间占比，就能估计「覆盖概率」。

examples.en: We compared the coverage probability with the nominal confidence level for each classroom method.
examples.zh: 我们将每种课堂方法的「覆盖概率」与名义置信水平相比较。

words.enDefinition: An endpoint of a confidence interval or a one-sided confidence bound.

examples.en: The confidence limit on the left marks the lower endpoint of this interval on the number line.
examples.zh: 数轴左侧的「置信限」是这个区间的下端点。

examples.en: We recorded each confidence limit after rounding both endpoints to the same decimal place.
examples.zh: 我们把两个端点都四舍五入到同一小数位，再记下各「置信限」。

words.enDefinition: The distance from an estimate to either endpoint of a symmetric confidence interval.

examples.en: The margin of error is the amount added to and subtracted from the estimate in this interval.
examples.zh: 在这个区间里，「误差限」就是估计值上下各加减的数值。

examples.en: We recalculated the margin of error after increasing the sample size in the classroom survey.
examples.zh: 我们增大课堂调查的样本量后，重新计算了「误差限」。

collocations: margin of error for an estimate

words.enDefinition: An upper or lower limit constructed to provide one-sided coverage for a parameter at a specified confidence level.

examples.en: The one-sided confidence bound gives only a lower limit for the population mean in our exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中的「单侧置信界」只给出总体均值的下限。

examples.en: We used a one-sided confidence bound because the worksheet asks how high the population mean might be.
examples.zh: 练习要求估计总体均值可能有多高，因此我们用了「单侧置信界」。

collocations: one-sided confidence bound for a mean

words.enDefinition: An interval designed to contain a future observation of the specified kind with a stated probability under the model.

examples.en: The prediction interval is wider here because the next observation can vary around the population mean.
examples.zh: 这个「预测区间」更宽，因为下一个观测值还会围绕总体均值波动。

examples.en: We compared a prediction interval for tomorrow's reading with a confidence interval for the average.
examples.zh: 我们比较了明天读数的「预测区间」和平均值的置信区间。

collocations: prediction interval for a new observation

words.enDefinition: An interval designed to cover at least a stated fraction of the population with a stated confidence level.

examples.en: The statistical tolerance interval targets a fraction of all lab readings rather than the mean alone.
examples.zh: 「统计容忍区间」以覆盖一定比例的实验读数为目标。

examples.en: We recorded both the target fraction and the confidence level for the statistical tolerance interval.
examples.zh: 我们为「统计容忍区间」同时记录了目标覆盖比例和置信水平。

words.enDefinition: An interval whose coverage approaches its target under stated conditions as the sample size grows.

examples.en: The asymptotic confidence interval uses a large-sample reference approximation for the estimate in this exercise.
examples.zh: 本练习的「渐近置信区间」对估计值采用大样本参考分布近似。

examples.en: We compared the asymptotic confidence interval with results from repeated small samples in the simulation.
examples.zh: 我们将「渐近置信区间」与模拟中反复抽取小样本得到的结果作了比较。

collocations: coverage of an asymptotic confidence interval

words.enDefinition: A confidence interval formed from an estimate plus or minus a reference quantile times its estimated standard error.

examples.en: The Wald interval in this example uses the observed sample proportion in its standard error.
examples.zh: 该示例中的「沃尔德区间」在计算标准误时使用观测样本比例。

examples.en: We examined a Wald interval whose lower endpoint falls below zero in the proportion exercise.
examples.zh: 我们在比例练习中考察了一个下端点低于零的「沃尔德区间」。

words.enDefinition: A binomial proportion interval obtained by inverting the score test for candidate probabilities.

examples.en: The Wilson score interval stays within the possible range of proportions in the small sample exercise.
examples.zh: 在小样本练习中，「威尔逊得分区间」落在比例的可能取值范围内。

examples.en: We compared the Wilson score interval with the simple normal approximation in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们将课堂示例的「威尔逊得分区间」与简单正态近似作了比较。

collocations: Wilson score interval for a proportion

words.enDefinition: A binomial proportion confidence interval based on exact tail probabilities, with coverage at least the nominal level.

examples.en: The Clopper-Pearson interval uses binomial probabilities directly for the small sample in our worksheet.
examples.zh: 「克洛珀—皮尔逊区间」对练习中的小样本直接使用二项分布概率。

examples.en: We compared the Clopper-Pearson interval with a shorter approximate interval for the same observed count.
examples.zh: 我们将同一观测计数的「克洛珀—皮尔逊区间」和一个更短的近似区间作了比较。

words.enDefinition: An estimate of a statistic's standard error obtained from its spread across bootstrap resamples.

examples.en: The bootstrap standard error is calculated from the spread of medians across classroom resamples.
examples.zh: 「自助法标准误」根据课堂各重抽样中位数的离散程度算出。

examples.en: We compared the bootstrap standard error with a formula-based estimate for the same statistic.
examples.zh: 我们把「自助法标准误」与同一统计量的基于公式的估计作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A confidence interval that uses chosen lower and upper quantiles of the bootstrap estimates as its endpoints.

examples.en: The percentile bootstrap interval takes both endpoints directly from the distribution of the resampled medians.
examples.zh: 「百分位自助法区间」直接从重抽样中位数的分布中取得两个端点。

examples.en: We plotted the percentile bootstrap interval after sorting the estimates from all the classroom resamples.
examples.zh: 我们对课堂各重抽样估计值排序后，画出了「百分位自助法区间」。

collocations: percentile bootstrap interval for a median

words.enDefinition: The default statistical claim used to determine the reference behaviour of a test statistic.

examples.en: The null hypothesis says that the two fictional groups have equal population mean scores.
examples.zh: 「原假设」认为，两个虚构组的总体平均成绩相等。

examples.en: We stated the null hypothesis before examining any differences in the classroom sample data.
examples.zh: 我们先写出「原假设」，再考察课堂样本数据里的差异。

words.enDefinition: A claim describing values or patterns that differ from what the null hypothesis states.

examples.en: The alternative hypothesis allows the fictional group means to differ in either direction in our exercise.
examples.zh: 练习的「备择假设」允许两个虚构组的总体均值在任一方向上存在差异。

examples.en: We chose the alternative hypothesis before calculating the statistic from the classroom observations.
examples.zh: 我们先选定「备择假设」，再用课堂观测值计算统计量。

words.enDefinition: A numerical quantity computed from the sample and compared with a reference distribution for a hypothesis test.

examples.en: The test statistic in our mean comparison is large when the difference is large relative to uncertainty.
examples.zh: 在这次均值比较中，差异相对其不确定性越大，「检验统计量」也越大。

examples.en: We calculated the test statistic and then located it on the reference distribution in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们算出「检验统计量」，再确定它在参考分布中的位置。

words.enDefinition: The sampling distribution of a test statistic when the null hypothesis and the test assumptions hold.

examples.en: The null distribution shows how large the statistic could be if the group means were equal.
examples.zh: 「原假设下的分布」显示两组均值相等时统计量可能取到多大的值。

examples.en: We simulated the null distribution before drawing the tail region used in the example test.
examples.zh: 我们先模拟「原假设下的分布」，再画出示例检验所用的尾部区域。

words.enDefinition: A cutoff on a reference distribution separating different decisions in a statistical test.

examples.en: The critical value divides the upper rejection tail from the remaining reference values in this test.
examples.zh: 本检验的「临界值」将上侧拒绝尾部与参考分布的其余部分隔开。

examples.en: We found the critical value from the table using the stated significance level in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们按给定显著性水平查表找出「临界值」。

words.enDefinition: The set of test-statistic values for which the procedure rejects the null hypothesis.

examples.en: The rejection region contains both tails in the classroom test with a two-sided alternative.
examples.zh: 课堂检验的备择假设为双侧，因此「拒绝域」包含两侧尾部。

examples.en: We shaded the rejection region before locating the calculated statistic on the reference curve.
examples.zh: 我们先给「拒绝域」加阴影，再确定算出的统计量在参考曲线上的位置。

words.enDefinition: The chosen maximum probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true under the test model.

examples.en: The significance level was specified before any classroom data were examined for differences between the groups.
examples.zh: 我们在查找课堂数据里的组间差异之前，就定好了「显著性水平」。

examples.en: We compared the reported probability with the significance level chosen for the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们将报告的概率与练习选定的「显著性水平」比较。

words.enDefinition: The probability, under the null model, of a test statistic at least as extreme as the observed statistic.

examples.en: The p-value includes outcomes at least as extreme as the observed statistic under the null model.
examples.zh: 「p 值」是在原假设模型下，统计量至少与观测值同样极端的概率。

examples.en: We computed the p-value from both tails because the alternative was two-sided in this exercise.
examples.zh: 由于这项练习采用双侧备择假设，我们从两侧尾部计算「p 值」。

words.enDefinition: A test whose alternative hypothesis specifies a departure in one direction only.

examples.en: The one-sided test examines whether the new process has a larger mean than the reference process.
examples.zh: 「单侧检验」考察新流程的均值是否大于参考流程的均值。

examples.en: We chose a one-sided test because the classroom question named a direction in advance.
examples.zh: 课堂题目预先指定了方向，因此我们选择「单侧检验」。

words.enDefinition: A test that can reject the null for sufficiently large departures in either direction.

examples.en: The two-sided test asks whether the mean differs from the reference value in either direction.
examples.zh: 「双侧检验」检验均值是否在任一方向上偏离参考值。

examples.en: We marked two tail regions to represent the rejection rule for the two-sided test.
examples.zh: 我们标出两侧尾部，表示「双侧检验」的拒绝规则。

words.enDefinition: The error of rejecting a true null hypothesis.

examples.en: A Type I error occurs when the test flags a difference although the fictional population means match.
examples.zh: 两个虚构总体均值实际相同，检验却判出差异时，就犯了「第一类错误」。

examples.en: We counted each Type I error across simulations where the null hypothesis was exactly true.
examples.zh: 我们统计原假设确实为真的各次模拟中出现的「第一类错误」。

collocations: probability of a Type I error
control the Type I error rate

words.enDefinition: The error of failing to reject the null hypothesis at a specified alternative that is true.

examples.en: A Type II error occurs when the test misses the difference built into the fictional data.
examples.zh: 检验没能检测出虚构数据中设定的差异时，就犯了「第二类错误」。

examples.en: We counted each Type II error in the classroom simulation using a fixed nonzero population difference.
examples.zh: 我们在固定非零总体差异的课堂模拟里，统计了每次「第二类错误」。

collocations: probability of a Type II error

words.enDefinition: The probability that a test rejects the null hypothesis under a specified alternative that is true.

examples.en: Statistical power increases in our simulation when the class uses more observations for the same difference.
examples.zh: 在相同差异下，全班使用更多观测值时，模拟的「统计功效」提高。

examples.en: We compared statistical power at two specified differences while holding the test procedure fixed.
examples.zh: 我们保持检验程序不变，比较两个指定差异对应的「统计功效」。

words.enDefinition: An analysis linking a statistical test's power to sample size, variability, significance level, and effect size.

examples.en: The power analysis helps the class choose a sample size for a specified difference in means.
examples.zh: 「功效分析」帮助全班为指定均值差选择样本量。

examples.en: We repeated the power analysis with greater assumed variability to see how the sample requirement changed.
examples.zh: 我们在假设变异更大的情况下重做「功效分析」，查看所需样本量如何变化。

words.enDefinition: The smallest effect size for which a specified test design is expected to reach a chosen power.

examples.en: The minimum detectable effect depends on sample size and the desired power in our classroom design.
examples.zh: 课堂设计中的「最小可检测效应」取决于样本量和目标功效。

examples.en: We estimated the minimum detectable effect before selecting how many observations to simulate in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先估计「最小可检测效应」，再选定要模拟的观测数。

collocations: minimum detectable effect for a study

words.expression: fail to reject the null hypothesis
words.lemma: fail to reject the null hypothesis
words.enDefinition: To conclude that the data do not meet the chosen test's rule for rejecting the null hypothesis.
acceptedEnVariants: fail to reject the null hypothesis

examples.en: We fail to reject the null hypothesis when the statistic stays outside the rejection region.
examples.zh: 统计量位于拒绝域外时，我们「未能拒绝原假设」。

examples.en: The students fail to reject the null hypothesis after comparing the statistic with the prespecified cutoff.
examples.zh: 学生将统计量与预先设定的临界值比较后，「未能拒绝原假设」。

collocations: fail to reject the null hypothesis at a chosen level
fail to reject the null hypothesis in the test
fail to reject the null hypothesis given the data

words.enDefinition: A graph showing how the probability of rejection changes across alternative parameter values for a given test design.

examples.en: The power curve shows that larger departures are easier to detect with the same classroom test.
examples.zh: 「功效曲线」显示，在同样的课堂检验下，较大的偏离更容易检测到。

examples.en: We used the power curve to compare two designs across a range of possible differences.
examples.zh: 我们用「功效曲线」比较两种设计在一系列可能差异下的表现。

words.enDefinition: The importance or usefulness of the estimated magnitude in the problem's real context.

examples.en: The class considered practical significance by comparing the small estimated difference with normal device variation.
examples.zh: 全班将估计得到的小差异与设备正常波动比较，以考虑其「实际意义」。

examples.en: We discussed practical significance even when the sample was large enough to detect a tiny difference.
examples.zh: 即便样本大到足以检测微小差异，我们也讨论了差异的「实际意义」。

words.enDefinition: A prespecified difference defining how far apart values may be and still count as practically equivalent.

examples.en: The equivalence margin defines the largest difference the classroom example treats as practically negligible.
examples.zh: 「等效界值」规定课堂示例中仍可视为实际可忽略的最大差异。

examples.en: We specified the equivalence margin before collecting readings from the two devices in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们在收集练习中两台设备的读数前，就定下了「等效界值」。

words.enDefinition: A test of one population mean using a standard normal reference when the population standard deviation is known under its model.

examples.en: The one-sample z-test compares the average calibration reading with the specified reference value in class.
examples.zh: 「单样本 z 检验」将课堂中的平均校准读数与指定参考值作比较。

examples.en: We used a one-sample z-test because the exercise supplied the population standard deviation and assumed normality.
examples.zh: 练习给出了总体标准差且假设总体正态，因此我们使用「单样本 z 检验」。

words.enDefinition: A test of one population mean using the sample standard deviation to estimate the standard error and a t reference distribution.

examples.en: The one-sample t-test compares the mean of the sample readings with the stated reference value.
examples.zh: 「单样本 t 检验」把样本读数的均值与给定参考值作比较。

examples.en: We used a one-sample t-test after checking the assumptions for the small classroom sample.
examples.zh: 我们检查小型课堂样本是否满足假设后，使用了「单样本 t 检验」。

words.zhGloss: 独立样本 t 检验
words.enDefinition: A t-based test for comparing two population means using samples with independent observations within and between the two groups.
acceptedZhAnswers: 独立样本 t 检验

examples.en: The independent-samples t-test compares average readings from two separately sampled sets of devices in class.
examples.zh: 「独立样本 t 检验」比较课堂上分别抽取的两组设备的平均读数。

examples.en: The groups were sampled independently with no shared devices, so we used an independent-samples t-test.
examples.zh: 两组独立抽取且没有共同设备，因此我们使用「独立样本 t 检验」。

words.zhGloss: 合并方差 t 检验
words.enDefinition: An independent-samples t-test that estimates a common population variance by pooling the two sample variances.
acceptedZhAnswers: 合并方差 t 检验

examples.en: The pooled-variance t-test uses a common variance estimate for the two groups on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 练习纸上的「合并方差 t 检验」为两组使用同一个方差估计值。

examples.en: We discussed the equal variance assumption before applying a pooled-variance t-test to the classroom data.
examples.zh: 将「合并方差 t 检验」应用于课堂数据前，我们先讨论了等方差假设。

words.enDefinition: A t-based test of two independent means that estimates the groups' variances separately and adjusts the reference degrees of freedom.

examples.en: Welch's t-test allows the two groups in the exercise to have different population variances.
examples.zh: 「韦尔奇 t 检验」允许练习中的两组具有不同的总体方差。

examples.en: We used Welch's t-test to compare means for the two independently sampled sets of readings.
examples.zh: 我们用「韦尔奇 t 检验」比较独立抽出的两组读数的均值。

collocations: degrees of freedom for Welch's t-test

words.enDefinition: A one-sample t-test applied to the within-pair differences of matched observations.

examples.en: The paired t-test uses the change in each device's reading before and after adjustment in our exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中的「配对 t 检验」使用各台设备调整前后读数的变化。

examples.en: We checked the differences for unusual values before carrying out the paired t-test in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先检查差值有没有异常值，再做「配对 t 检验」。

words.enDefinition: The subtraction of two observations that belong to the same matched pair, in a consistent order across pairs.

examples.en: We calculated a paired difference for each weighing device using the second reading minus the first.
examples.zh: 我们用第二次读数减第一次读数，为每台称重设备计算「配对差值」。

examples.en: The paired difference is negative for the device that produced a lower reading on remeasurement.
examples.zh: 重新测量后读数较低的那台设备，其「配对差值」为负。

words.enDefinition: The assumption that specified observations, differences, or errors follow a normal distribution in a statistical method.

examples.en: The normality assumption for this paired test concerns the measured differences within each device pair.
examples.zh: 这个配对检验的「正态性假设」针对各设备配对的实测差值。

examples.en: We discussed why the normality assumption matters more for the exact small-sample result in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们讨论了为什么「正态性假设」对精确的小样本结果更加重要。

words.enDefinition: The assumption that the groups' population variances are the same for a comparison procedure.

examples.en: The equal variance assumption is required by the pooled comparison used in the first exercise.
examples.zh: 第一道练习所用的合并方差比较要求满足「等方差假设」。

examples.en: We discussed whether the different simulated spreads make the equal variance assumption plausible in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们讨论了各组模拟数据的离散程度不同，「等方差假设」是否可信。

collocations: violation of the equal variance assumption
rely on the equal variance assumption

words.zhGloss: 韦尔奇—萨特思韦特自由度
words.enDefinition: An approximate reference degrees-of-freedom value calculated from sample sizes and variance estimates for an unequal-variance comparison.
acceptedZhAnswers: 韦尔奇—萨特思韦特自由度

examples.en: The Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom need not be a whole number in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 课堂示例里的「韦尔奇—萨特思韦特自由度」可以不是整数。

examples.en: We computed the Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom before looking up the approximate reference value.
examples.zh: 我们先算出「韦尔奇—萨特思韦特自由度」，再查近似参考值。

words.enDefinition: A large-sample test comparing one observed proportion with a specified population proportion using a standard normal reference.

examples.en: The one-proportion z-test compares the fraction of acceptable pieces with the specified target in our exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中的「单比例 z 检验」将合格零件比例与指定目标作比较。

examples.en: We checked the expected counts before using the one-proportion z-test for the simulated production sample.
examples.zh: 我们检查预期计数后，对模拟生产样本做「单比例 z 检验」。

words.enDefinition: A large-sample test comparing two population proportions using independent samples and a standard normal reference.

examples.en: The two-proportion z-test compares the fraction of acceptable pieces from two fictional production lines in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上的「双比例 z 检验」比较两条虚构生产线的合格零件比例。

examples.en: We checked the independence of the two samples before carrying out the two-proportion z-test in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们确认两个样本独立后，再做「双比例 z 检验」。

words.enDefinition: The combined success count divided by the combined sample size, used to estimate a common proportion under a null hypothesis.

examples.en: The pooled proportion uses both samples because the null hypothesis gives them a common success probability.
examples.zh: 「合并比例」使用两个样本，因为原假设赋予两者相同的成功概率。

examples.en: We calculated the pooled proportion before computing the null standard error in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 课堂练习中，我们先算「合并比例」，再算原假设下的标准误。

words.enDefinition: A test of a binomial success probability based directly on the binomial distribution.

examples.en: The exact binomial test uses the observed number of successes in the small classroom sample.
examples.zh: 「精确二项检验」使用课堂小样本中观测到的成功次数。

examples.en: We used an exact binomial test because the exercise asks for probabilities without a normal approximation.
examples.zh: 练习要求直接求概率，因此我们使用「精确二项检验」。

collocations: p-value from an exact binomial test

words.enDefinition: A test comparing one population variance with a specified value using a chi-square reference under independent normal sampling.

examples.en: The chi-square test for a variance compares the spread of readings with a stated population benchmark.
examples.zh: 「方差的卡方检验」把读数的离散程度与给定的总体基准作比较。

examples.en: We checked the normal model before using the chi-square test for a variance in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先检查正态模型，再使用「方差的卡方检验」。

collocations: perform a chi-square test for a variance
reference value in a chi-square test for a variance
assumptions of a chi-square test for a variance

words.enDefinition: A test comparing observed category counts with expected counts under a specified probability model.

examples.en: The chi-square goodness-of-fit test compares the observed colour counts with the distribution stated for the exercise.
examples.zh: 「卡方拟合优度检验」比较各颜色的观测计数与练习指定分布下的计数。

examples.en: We found the expected counts before carrying out the chi-square goodness-of-fit test on the simulated draws.
examples.zh: 我们先求预期计数，再对模拟抽取得到的数据做「卡方拟合优度检验」。

collocations: assumptions of a chi-square goodness-of-fit test
statistic for a chi-square goodness-of-fit test

words.enDefinition: A test of whether two categorical variables are independent in the population represented by a contingency table.

examples.en: The chi-square test of independence examines whether the selected categories are associated in the fabricated class survey.
examples.zh: 「卡方独立性检验」考察虚构课堂调查中的选定类别变量是否相关。

examples.en: We inspected the expected cell counts before interpreting the chi-square test of independence in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先核对各单元格预期计数，再解释「卡方独立性检验」。

collocations: perform a chi-square test of independence
assumptions of a chi-square test of independence
report a chi-square test of independence

words.enDefinition: A test of whether independently sampled populations have the same distribution over the categories of an outcome.

examples.en: The chi-square test of homogeneity compares response categories across independently sampled schools in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中的「卡方同质性检验」比较独立抽取的各学校的回答类别分布。

examples.en: We used a chi-square test of homogeneity to compare the colour distributions in three simulated batches.
examples.zh: 我们使用「卡方同质性检验」比较三个模拟批次的颜色分布。

collocations: perform a chi-square test of homogeneity
compare populations with a chi-square test of homogeneity
assumptions of a chi-square test of homogeneity

words.enDefinition: The count predicted for a table cell under the null probability model.

examples.en: The expected cell count uses the row and column totals in the classroom independence test.
examples.zh: 课堂独立性检验用行合计与列合计计算「单元格期望频数」。

examples.en: We compared each expected cell count with the corresponding observed count in the practice table.
examples.zh: 我们把练习表的每个「单元格期望频数」与对应的实测频数作了比较。

words.enDefinition: In count tables, the observed count minus its expected count, divided by the square root of the expected count.

examples.en: The Pearson residual is positive when a cell has more observations than the model expects.
examples.zh: 某单元格的观测频数大于模型预期时，「皮尔逊残差」为正。

examples.en: We examined each Pearson residual to identify the largest departures in the classroom table.
examples.zh: 我们查看各个「皮尔逊残差」，找出课堂表格中偏离最大的单元格。

words.enDefinition: A test comparing two population variances using their sample variance ratio and an F reference for independent normal samples.

examples.en: The F-test for equal variances uses the ratio of the two sample variances in our worksheet.
examples.zh: 练习里的「等方差 F 检验」使用两个样本方差之比。

examples.en: We checked the distributional assumptions before applying the F-test for equal variances to the classroom example.
examples.zh: 对课堂示例做「等方差 F 检验」前，我们核查了分布假设。

collocations: apply an F-test for equal variances
assumptions of an F-test for equal variances
report an F-test for equal variances

words.enDefinition: A test of equal group variances based on differences among groups in absolute deviations from group centres.

examples.en: Levene's test compares absolute deviations from group means in the version shown on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 练习纸所用版本的「莱文检验」比较各组观测值与本组均值的绝对偏差。

examples.en: We used Levene's test to check whether the three simulated groups had comparable spreads in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们用「莱文检验」核查三个模拟组的离散程度是否相近。

words.enDefinition: A version of Levene's variance test that computes absolute deviations from each group's median.

examples.en: The Brown-Forsythe test uses group medians as reference points for the deviations in our exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中的「布朗—福赛斯检验」以各组中位数为计算偏差的基准。

examples.en: We compared the Brown-Forsythe test with the version based on group means in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们将「布朗—福赛斯检验」与练习纸上基于各组均值的版本作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A procedure for testing whether population means are equal across levels of one grouping factor.

examples.en: The one-way analysis of variance compares mean calibration readings across three simulated methods in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中的「单因素方差分析」比较三种模拟方法的平均校准读数。

examples.en: We used one-way analysis of variance because the worksheet groups the scores by one factor.
examples.zh: 练习按一个因素将成绩分组，因此我们使用「单因素方差分析」。

collocations: perform a one-way analysis of variance
assumptions of one-way analysis of variance

words.enDefinition: The sum of squared deviations of group means from the overall mean, weighted by group sizes.

examples.en: We calculated the between-group sum of squares after finding each group mean and the overall mean.
examples.zh: 我们先求各组均值和总均值，再算「组间平方和」。

examples.en: The between-group sum of squares increases when the simulated group means move apart in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，各组模拟均值之间的距离增大时，「组间平方和」也增大。

collocations: calculate the between-group sum of squares
report the between-group sum of squares

words.enDefinition: The sum of squared deviations of each observation from its own group's mean.

examples.en: The within-group sum of squares measures spread around separate group averages in the classroom data.
examples.zh: 「组内平方和」衡量课堂数据围绕各自组均值的离散程度。

examples.en: We found the within-group sum of squares before dividing by the corresponding degrees of freedom.
examples.zh: 我们先算出「组内平方和」，再除以相应自由度。

collocations: calculate the within-group sum of squares
report the within-group sum of squares

words.enDefinition: A sum of squares divided by its associated degrees of freedom in an analysis of variance.

examples.en: The mean square is obtained by dividing the worksheet's sum of squares by its degrees of freedom.
examples.zh: 「均方」用练习表中的平方和除以相应自由度得到。

examples.en: We calculated each mean square before forming the ratio used in the classroom comparison.
examples.zh: 我们算出各个「均方」，再构造课堂比较所用的比值。

words.zhGloss: 方差分析 F 统计量
words.enDefinition: The ratio of a model or group mean square to its error mean square in an analysis of variance.
acceptedZhAnswers: 方差分析 F 统计量

examples.en: The ANOVA F statistic is large when differences among group means dominate within-group variability in this example.
examples.zh: 示例中，组均值之间的差异相较组内变异很大，因此「方差分析 F 统计量」也较大。

examples.en: We compared the ANOVA F statistic with its reference distribution after reading both degrees of freedom.
examples.zh: 我们先读取两个自由度，再把「方差分析 F 统计量」与参考分布比较。

collocations: reference distribution of the ANOVA F statistic

words.enDefinition: A table summarizing sources of variation, degrees of freedom, sums of squares, and associated test quantities.

examples.en: The ANOVA table has separate rows for variation between groups and variation within groups in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习的「方差分析表」用不同行列出组间变异和组内变异。

examples.en: We used the ANOVA table to find the error degrees of freedom for the comparison.
examples.zh: 我们用「方差分析表」找到此次比较的误差自由度。

collocations: error row of an ANOVA table

words.enDefinition: A test of a joint hypothesis, such as equality across several means, without specifying which comparison accounts for rejection.

examples.en: The omnibus test asks whether all three group means are equal in the simulated example.
examples.zh: 模拟示例中的「总体检验」考察三个组均值是否全部相等。

examples.en: After the omnibus test, we examined which pairs might explain the departure in the classroom data.
examples.zh: 做完「总体检验」后，我们考察课堂数据中哪些组间配对可能解释这种偏离。

collocations: follow an omnibus test with comparisons

words.enDefinition: An analysis-of-variance procedure for comparing group means without assuming equal population variances.

examples.en: Welch's ANOVA compares mean readings across three independently sampled groups with different spreads in this exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中的「韦尔奇方差分析」比较三个独立抽取、离散程度各异的组的平均读数。

examples.en: We discussed which reference degrees of freedom Welch's ANOVA uses for the simulated classroom data.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「韦尔奇方差分析」为课堂模拟数据采用哪个参考自由度。

words.enDefinition: A follow-up comparison selected after examining the data or results of an overall test, often with adjustment for multiple comparisons.

examples.en: The post hoc comparison examines two production methods after the overall test shows differences among the means.
examples.zh: 总体检验发现均值存在差异后，「事后比较」进一步考察其中两种生产方法。

examples.en: We recorded the adjustment used for each post hoc comparison in the classroom results table.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂结果表里记录了每项「事后比较」所用的校正方法。

words.enDefinition: Observations linked in pairs by a common unit or a matching rule and analysed through their pairing.

examples.en: The paired observations come from the same simulated device measured before and after adjustment in class.
examples.zh: 这组「配对观测值」来自课堂同一模拟设备调整前后的测量。

examples.en: We kept the recorded identifiers so the paired observations could be lined up correctly for analysis.
examples.zh: 我们保留了记录的标识符，让「配对观测值」在分析时能正确对应。

words.enDefinition: A test that uses the relative ordering of observations to form its statistic.

examples.en: The rank-based test compares the positions of readings after the two classroom samples are combined.
examples.zh: 「基于秩的检验」在合并两组课堂样本后比较各读数的排序位置。

examples.en: We used a rank-based test because the exercise asks us to compare ordered observations.
examples.zh: 练习要求比较排过序的观测值，因此我们使用「基于秩的检验」。

words.enDefinition: The total of the ranks assigned to observations in one group of a pooled ranking.

examples.en: The rank sum for the first group includes each of its positions in the combined ordering.
examples.zh: 第一组的「秩和」将该组在合并排序中的所有名次相加。

examples.en: We calculated the rank sum before comparing it with the values expected under the null.
examples.zh: 我们先算出「秩和」，再与原假设下预期的数值比较。

words.enDefinition: The mean of the rank positions that a set of tied observations would otherwise occupy.

examples.en: The average rank for ties is shared by both observations that have the same reading.
examples.zh: 读数相同的两个观测值共用「并列值的平均秩」。

examples.en: We assigned the average rank for ties before adding the positions within each group.
examples.zh: 在对各组名次求和前，我们先为并列项赋予「并列值的平均秩」。

collocations: assign an average rank for ties
calculate the average rank for ties
use an average rank for ties

words.enDefinition: A test based on counts of positive and negative deviations or paired differences, excluding zeros.

examples.en: The sign test counts how often the second classroom reading exceeds the first for each device.
examples.zh: 「符号检验」统计各台设备第二次课堂读数超过第一次的次数。

examples.en: We excluded zero differences before applying the sign test in the paired measurement exercise.
examples.zh: 在配对测量练习中，我们先去掉零差值，再应用「符号检验」。

words.zhGloss: 威尔科克森符号秩检验
words.enDefinition: A test of the centre of a symmetric difference distribution using ranks of absolute differences together with their signs.
acceptedZhAnswers: 威尔科克森符号秩检验

examples.en: The Wilcoxon signed-rank test ranks the absolute paired differences before attaching their original signs in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上的「威尔科克森符号秩检验」先对配对差值的绝对值排序，再加回各自原有的正负号。

examples.en: We discussed symmetry of the differences before interpreting the Wilcoxon signed-rank test in the exercise.
examples.zh: 解读练习中的「威尔科克森符号秩检验」前，我们先讨论差值分布的对称性。

collocations: assumptions of a Wilcoxon signed-rank test

words.zhGloss: 曼—惠特尼 U 检验
words.enDefinition: A rank-based test comparing two independent groups, with a location interpretation under additional distributional assumptions.
acceptedZhAnswers: 曼—惠特尼 U 检验

examples.en: The Mann-Whitney U test ranks both groups together before assessing whether one tends to yield higher readings.
examples.zh: 「曼—惠特尼 U 检验」先将两组一起排序，再评估其中一组的读数是否往往较高。

examples.en: We discussed when a Mann-Whitney U test could be interpreted as a comparison of locations.
examples.zh: 我们讨论在什么条件下「曼—惠特尼 U 检验」可以解释为位置比较。

collocations: assumptions of a Mann-Whitney U test

words.zhGloss: 克鲁斯卡尔—沃利斯检验
words.enDefinition: A rank-based test for independent groups whose null hypothesis is a common outcome distribution. A location comparison requires additional assumptions.
acceptedZhAnswers: 克鲁斯卡尔—沃利斯检验

examples.en: The Kruskal-Wallis test compares ranks across three independently sampled groups in the simulated calibration example.
examples.zh: 模拟校准示例里的「克鲁斯卡尔—沃利斯检验」比较三个独立样本组的秩。

examples.en: After the Kruskal-Wallis test, we considered which group comparisons would require a separate analysis.
examples.zh: 做完「克鲁斯卡尔—沃利斯检验」后，我们考虑哪些组别比较需要另行分析。

words.enDefinition: A rank-based test comparing conditions by ranking observations within each matched group or block.

examples.en: The Friedman test ranks the three methods within each device before combining evidence across devices.
examples.zh: 「弗里德曼检验」先在每台设备内对三种方法排序，再合并各设备的证据。

examples.en: We used a Friedman test because each classroom block contains readings under every condition.
examples.zh: 课堂中每个区组都有所有条件下的读数，因此我们用「弗里德曼检验」。

words.enDefinition: The ordinary correlation computed on the ranks of paired values, measuring monotonic association.

examples.en: Spearman rank correlation is positive when longer study times generally correspond to higher test scores.
examples.zh: 较长的学习时间通常对应较高的测试分数时，「斯皮尔曼秩相关」为正。

examples.en: We calculated Spearman rank correlation to assess whether the two variables tended to increase together.
examples.zh: 我们计算「斯皮尔曼秩相关」，评估两个变量是否倾向于一起增大。

words.enDefinition: A rank association measure based on the balance of concordant and discordant pairs.

examples.en: Kendall's tau is positive when more pairs agree than disagree in their relative ordering here.
examples.zh: 在本例中，相对顺序一致的观测值对多于不一致的值对时，「肯德尔 τ 系数」为正。

examples.en: We computed Kendall's tau after reviewing how the version used in the exercise handles ties.
examples.zh: 我们先查看练习所用版本如何处理并列，再计算「肯德尔 τ 系数」。

words.zhGloss: 单样本柯尔莫哥洛夫—斯米尔诺夫检验
words.enDefinition: A goodness-of-fit test based on the greatest gap between an empirical and a fully specified reference cumulative distribution.
acceptedZhAnswers: 单样本柯尔莫哥洛夫—斯米尔诺夫检验

examples.en: The one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test uses the largest gap between the two cumulative curves in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上的「单样本柯尔莫哥洛夫—斯米尔诺夫检验」使用两条累积分布曲线的最大间距。

examples.en: We used a one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test with the reference distribution specified before looking at the data.
examples.zh: 我们使用「单样本柯尔莫哥洛夫—斯米尔诺夫检验」，并在查看数据前指定了参考分布。

collocations: reference distribution for a one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
assumptions of a one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test

words.enDefinition: A test that compares an observed statistic with values obtained by allowable rearrangements under the null hypothesis.

examples.en: The permutation test rearranges the group labels while holding the classroom readings fixed in the example.
examples.zh: 示例的「置换检验」重新排列组标签，同时保持课堂读数不变。

examples.en: We explained which rearrangements the permutation test allows before counting values as extreme as the result.
examples.zh: 我们先说明「置换检验」允许哪些重排，再统计至少与结果同样极端的数值。

words.enDefinition: The distribution of a statistic over the rearrangements permitted under a permutation test's null hypothesis.

examples.en: The permutation distribution contains the group mean difference for each valid arrangement of labels in class.
examples.zh: 课堂的「置换分布」包含每种有效标签排列对应的组均值差。

examples.en: We compared our observed difference with the tails of the permutation distribution in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习时，我们将观测差异与「置换分布」的尾部作比较。

words.enDefinition: The property that specified rearrangements leave the relevant joint distribution unchanged under the model.

examples.en: Exchangeability under the null lets us rearrange labels in this independent and identically distributed classroom example.
examples.zh: 在这个独立同分布的课堂示例中，原假设下的「可交换性」允许我们重排标签。

examples.en: We discussed why exchangeability might fail if the two groups have different variability in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了练习中两组变异程度不同时，「可交换性」为何可能不成立。

words.enDefinition: A test of association in a contingency table using the exact conditional distribution for fixed margins.

examples.en: Fisher's exact test evaluates the small table with the row and column totals held fixed.
examples.zh: 「费希尔精确检验」在行合计和列合计固定的情况下检验这个小表。

examples.en: We used Fisher's exact test after noting the small counts in the two by two table.
examples.zh: 注意到二乘二表的频数较小后，我们使用了「费希尔精确检验」。

words.enDefinition: A test of whether paired binary responses have the same marginal proportions, based on discordant pairs.

examples.en: McNemar's test counts the pairs that change classification between the first and second readings in class.
examples.zh: 「麦克尼马尔检验」统计课堂里第一次和第二次读数的分类不一致的配对。

examples.en: We used McNemar's test because the two binary classifications came from the same simulated devices.
examples.zh: 由于两次二元分类来自同一批模拟设备，我们使用了「麦克尼马尔检验」。

words.enDefinition: A test for nonrandom ordering that compares the number of consecutive runs with its reference behaviour.

examples.en: The runs test counts stretches of the same sign in the worksheet's sequence of differences.
examples.zh: 「游程检验」统计练习纸的差值序列里同号连续出现的段数。

examples.en: We kept the original observation order before applying the runs test to the classroom sequence.
examples.zh: 对课堂序列做「游程检验」前，我们保留了观测的原始顺序。

words.enDefinition: A set of statistical comparisons considered together because their combined error properties matter.

examples.en: The exercise treats the mean differences as multiple comparisons because all pairwise results will be reported together.
examples.zh: 练习把这些均值差异视为「多重比较」，因为所有两两比较结果都会一起报告。

examples.en: We planned how to handle multiple comparisons before looking at the results for each device.
examples.zh: 我们在查看各设备结果前，就计划好如何处理「多重比较」。

words.enDefinition: A group of related hypotheses that are treated together when assessing combined statistical errors.

examples.en: The family of hypotheses includes all preselected comparisons of mean readings in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 「假设族」包括课堂练习中预先选定的所有读数均值比较。

examples.en: We defined the family of hypotheses before choosing the method for adjusting the reported p-values in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先界定「假设族」，再选择校正报告 p 值的方法。

words.enDefinition: The probability of making at least one false rejection within a family of tested hypotheses.

examples.en: The family-wise error rate concerns whether even one incorrect rejection occurs across the planned tests.
examples.zh: 「族错误率」关注计划中的一系列检验是否至少发生一次错误拒绝。

examples.en: We compared the family-wise error rate under two adjustment procedures in the classroom simulation.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂模拟中比较两种校正程序的「族错误率」。

collocations: family-wise error rate for a group of tests

words.enDefinition: The expected fraction of false rejections among all rejections, counted as zero when none occur.

examples.en: The false discovery rate averages the share of incorrect discoveries across repeated classroom simulations of multiple tests.
examples.zh: 「错误发现率」是多重检验课堂模拟反复运行时，错误发现所占比例的平均值。

examples.en: We discussed how controlling the false discovery rate differs from guarding against any false rejection.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了控制「错误发现率」与防范任何一次错误拒绝的不同。

words.enDefinition: A p-value modified to account for a specified multiple-testing procedure and set of hypotheses.

examples.en: The adjusted p-value reflects that the group comparison is one of several on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 「校正后的 p 值」考虑到该组间比较只是练习中多项比较的一项。

examples.en: We reported each adjusted p-value alongside its unadjusted counterpart in the classroom results table.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂结果表里，将每个「校正后的 p 值」与其未校正值并列报告。

collocations: compare an adjusted p-value with a threshold

words.enDefinition: A correction that divides the family significance level by the number of tests to limit family-wise error.

examples.en: The Bonferroni correction uses a smaller threshold for each of the five planned tests in class.
examples.zh: 对于课堂计划中的五项检验，「邦费罗尼校正」给每项使用更小的阈值。

examples.en: We applied the Bonferroni correction before interpreting which of the classroom comparisons met the adjusted threshold.
examples.zh: 我们先应用「邦费罗尼校正」，再解释哪些课堂比较达到了校正后的阈值。

words.enDefinition: A step-down adjustment that tests ordered p-values against successive thresholds to control family-wise error.

examples.en: The Holm correction begins with the smallest p-value in the set of classroom comparisons.
examples.zh: 「霍尔姆校正」从这组课堂比较中最小的 p 值开始。

examples.en: We applied the Holm correction and stopped when an ordered p-value failed its threshold.
examples.zh: 我们应用「霍尔姆校正」，在某个排序后的 p 值未达到对应阈值时停止。

words.zhGloss: 本杰明尼—霍赫贝格程序
words.enDefinition: A step-up multiple-testing method that controls the false discovery rate under independence or certain dependence conditions.
acceptedZhAnswers: 本杰明尼—霍赫贝格程序

examples.en: The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure compares ordered p-values with rank-dependent thresholds in our classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 课堂练习中的「本杰明尼—霍赫贝格程序」将排序后的 p 值与随名次变化的阈值比较。

examples.en: We stated the conditions for using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure before interpreting the selected findings in class.
examples.zh: 解读课堂中筛出的发现之前，我们先写明采用「本杰明尼—霍赫贝格程序」的条件。

words.enDefinition: A procedure that compares all pairs of group means while controlling family-wise error under its model assumptions.

examples.en: Tukey's HSD test compares every pair of mean readings from the three fictional production methods.
examples.zh: 「图基 HSD 检验」对三种虚构生产方法的平均读数做所有两两比较。

examples.en: We used Tukey's HSD test to report which pairs differed in the simulated classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们用「图基 HSD 检验」报告模拟课堂示例中哪些组间配对存在差异。

collocations: Tukey's HSD test for pairwise comparisons

words.enDefinition: A set of intervals designed to cover all corresponding parameters together at a stated overall confidence level.

examples.en: The simultaneous confidence intervals are wider here because they are designed to cover all pairwise differences together.
examples.zh: 这里的「同时置信区间」更宽，因为其设计是同时覆盖全部两两差异。

examples.en: We reported simultaneous confidence intervals when presenting the full set of classroom comparisons on one chart.
examples.zh: 我们用一张图展示整组课堂比较时，报告了「同时置信区间」。

words.enDefinition: A preselected weighted comparison of group means, with weights summing to zero.

examples.en: The planned contrast compares the average of two group means with a reference group's mean.
examples.zh: 「预设对比」将两个组均值的平均值与参考组均值比较。

examples.en: We specified the planned contrast before looking at the observed differences in the classroom measurements.
examples.zh: 我们在查看课堂测量的观测差异前，就确定了「预设对比」。

words.enDefinition: The comparisons formed by taking every distinct pair of groups in an analysis.

examples.en: All pairwise comparisons produce three differences when the classroom exercise includes exactly three groups.
examples.zh: 课堂练习恰有三组时，「全部两两比较」产生三个差异。

examples.en: We listed all pairwise comparisons before deciding how to adjust the associated tests in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先列出「全部两两比较」，再决定如何校正对应的检验。

words.enDefinition: A multiple-comparison procedure that compares several group means with a common control mean.

examples.en: Dunnett's test compares each proposed calibration method with the same reference method in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中的「邓尼特检验」把各拟议校准方法分别与同一种参考方法比较。

examples.en: We used Dunnett's test because the classroom question asks only about differences from the control.
examples.zh: 课堂题目只问各组与对照的差异，因此我们使用「邓尼特检验」。

collocations: use Dunnett's test for control comparisons

words.enDefinition: An equivalence procedure that tests both sides of a specified equivalence range and requires both tests to reject.
acceptedEnVariants: equivalence test by two one-sided tests

examples.en: The two one-sided tests procedure requires rejecting both null hypotheses before declaring equivalence within the prespecified limits.
examples.zh: 「双单侧检验法」必须拒绝两个原假设，才能判定差异落在预设的等效界值内。

examples.en: We used the two one-sided tests procedure to evaluate equivalence in the simulated calibration exercise.
examples.zh: 我们在模拟校准练习中用「双单侧检验法」检验等效性。

collocations: apply the two one-sided tests procedure
assumptions of the two one-sided tests procedure
use the two one-sided tests procedure

words.enDefinition: A change to thresholds, p-values, or intervals to meet a chosen error criterion when analysing several hypotheses.

examples.en: The multiplicity adjustment changes the thresholds because the classroom report includes several separate tests.
examples.zh: 由于课堂报告包含多项独立列出的检验，「多重性校正」改变了各项阈值。

examples.en: We specified the multiplicity adjustment before examining the simulated comparisons of average device readings.
examples.zh: 我们在查看模拟设备平均读数的比较结果前，就指定了「多重性校正」。
